This is something I have been trying to do for a good while, and I finally got it to work after...more time than I will admit.

First, we need to make a bash script:

if [ ! -x /usr/bin/cmus-remote ];
then
echo "cmus is not installed."
exit
fi

ARTIST=$( cmus-remote -Q 2>/dev/null | grep artist | cut -d " " -f 3- )
TITLE=$( cmus-remote -Q 2>/dev/null | grep title | cut -d " " -f 3- )

if [ -z "$ARTIST" ];
then
echo "Nothing"
else
echo "$ARTIST - $TITLE"
fi

Save this in /usr/bin with a simple name that you will remember, I named mine "conc" for "conky cmus". It doesn't matter what you name it, and you do not need to put ".sh" at the end (in facts, it's better not to). Also, the part that says 

echo "Nothing"

Will always be displaying "Nothing" when cmus is not playing music, so feel free to change the word Nothing to something witty if you want.

Now fire up your favorite editor and open your .conkyrc, and add the following wherever you want:

${execi 2 /usr/bin/conc}

If you didn't name your script "conc", or save it in /usr/bin, be sure to correct the line to match your script name and path. Now, fire up cmus and enter the following:

:set status_display_program=/usr/bin/conc

Now, you should be able to hit play and watch as conky immediately changes "Nothing" to:

Artist - Song Name
